name: apple pie
instructions:
American apple pie with a beurre-manie-thickened filling and a two-temperature bake for the open-faced format. (Tarte tatin is the french equivalent — different dish; will live separately when written.)

=== FILLING INGREDIENTS ===
- 4 apples (honey crisp — or a honey-crisp-plus-green mix for a mix of sweet and tart)
- 1 tsp vanilla
- 1/2 tsp cinnamon
- pinch of nutmeg
- pinch of cardamom
- zest of 1 lemon
- juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/2 cup brown sugar
- 1/2 to 1 tbsp granulated sugar
- BEURRE MANIE: mostly butter with a smaller amount of flour — should be LIQUID, not playdough consistency. Salt to taste (aim for salted-butter salinity — this is the whole reason a sweet pie needs salt).

=== PASTRY + FINISH ===
- 1 single unbaked sweet pie crust
- egg wash or cream wash for the crust

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Preheat oven to 425°F.
2. Prep the apples: peel, core, slice.
3. In a bowl, toss the apples with vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, cardamom, lemon zest, lemon juice, brown sugar, and granulated sugar.
4. MAKE THE BEURRE MANIE: soften butter well and mash together with a smaller amount of flour. Salt to taste. Should be pourable / liquid, NOT playdough consistency (too much flour is a failure mode — see notes). Fold the beurre manie into the apple filling.
5. Turn the filling into an unbaked sweet pie crust.
6. CREAM OR EGG WASH the exposed crust — this is what browns the pastry properly.
7. FIRST BAKE (TOAST THE CRUST): bake at 425°F to toast the crust.
8. SECOND BAKE (STEAM THE APPLES): cover the pie loosely with aluminum foil and drop the oven to 375°F. Bake covered for 20 minutes — this steams the apples through without over-browning the top.
9. THIRD BAKE (UNCOVER): uncover and bake the rest of the way at 375°F until the apples are tender and the top is deeply golden.
10. Cool before slicing.

COVERED-STAGE NOTE: the covered-steam stage is for the OPEN-FACED format. For a CLOSED (double-crust) pie, the top crust already traps steam, and the covered stage is unnecessary — go 425°F → uncovered-at-375°F straight through.
notes:
=== APPLE CHOICE — HONEY CRISP OR HONEY CRISP + GREEN MIX ===

Honey crisp alone works — sweet, holds shape, doesn't break down to applesauce. A mix of honey crisp + green apple (granny smith) gives you a sweet-and-tart balance where the greens add acidity and firmness against the honey crisp's sweetness.

=== BEURRE MANIE — MOSTLY BUTTER, LIQUID NOT PLAYDOUGH, SALT AS IF SALTED BUTTER ===

The beurre manie is the thickener and enrichment for the filling. Critical technique notes:

- MOSTLY BUTTER, WITH LESS FLOUR THAN INSTINCT SUGGESTS: standard beurre-manie ratios (equal parts butter and flour) are wrong here. This one should be mostly butter with a smaller amount of flour worked in.
- LIQUID, NOT PLAYDOUGH: the finished beurre manie should be pourable / liquid, not a stiff clay-like mass you can shape by hand. Playdough consistency means too much flour has gone in.
- SALT TO TASTE (AS IF USING SALTED BUTTER): the beurre manie should read salted, at roughly the salinity you'd get from salted butter. Salt is what keeps a sweet apple pie from reading one-note-sugary — the salt in the beurre manie is why unsalted butter here needs added salt.

=== TWO-TEMPERATURE BAKE + COVERED-STEAM STAGE (OPEN-FACED VERSION) ===

The open-faced version uses three baking stages:
1. 425°F to toast the crust (crust needs the higher heat to color properly before the filling drives things wet).
2. 375°F COVERED with aluminum foil for 20 min to steam the apples through (protects the already-toasted crust from over-browning while the apples finish).
3. 375°F UNCOVERED for the rest to finish coloring and drive off residual moisture.

CLOSED-PIE VERSION SKIPS THE COVERED STAGE: with a top crust in place, the pie already has a steam trap over the filling. Covering with foil on top of a closed crust is redundant. Go 425°F to toast → drop to 375°F uncovered straight through.

=== CREAM OR EGG WASH THE CRUST — NON-OPTIONAL ===

Brush the exposed crust with cream or egg wash before the first bake. This is what gives the pastry its deep golden brown color. Skipping it leaves a pale, undercooked-looking crust even after the full bake — the pastry cooks but doesn't brown properly.

=== FAILURE MODES ENCOUNTERED SO FAR ===

- TOO MUCH FLOUR IN THE BEURRE MANIE: the beurre manie ends up playdough-consistency, and the filling reads pasty/floury rather than buttery-and-lightly-thickened. Fix: less flour next time — the ratio should be mostly butter. It's easier to correct too-thin than too-thick.
- NO COVERED STAGE IN THE OPEN-FACE VERSION: the apples don't cook through properly without the steam trap, and the top of the exposed filling can over-brown while the interior stays firm. The 20 min at 375°F covered is what actually cooks the apples in the open-faced format — skipping it leaves the pie under-cooked in the middle even after a long bake.
